useResendCooldown ships at src/features/auth/useResendCooldown.ts and both OTP forms gate resend on resendIn > 0. Row is stale. Panel throttle still the real bound.

handleLogout now dispatches clearOfflineCart alongside clearCart and clearRecentlyViewed. The sync-failure branch still keeps items on purpose - clearing there would discard a guest cart on a transient failure; needs an owner call.

Verified end to end. The order path never trusts the callback - OrderPaymentView onSuccess only sets phase waiting then polls getSpecificOrders until the panel reports payment_status completed which the webhook sets. The wallet path re-reads the balance from the server through updateUserDataInRedux. Panel side both webhooks verify an HMAC over the raw body with hash_equals and dedupe on ProcessedWebhookEvent. Residual - the wallet success toast fires before the balance is confirmed so it can read Recharged while the webhook is still in flight; cosmetic only.
Fixed by deleting the dead WithdrawModal - the component had no render site anywhere in src. deductBalance remains in services/wallet.ts as an unused endpoint wrapper with no flaw of its own.

ReturnSheet now runs every picked file through rejectImage - mime allowlist excluding SVG plus a 5MB ceiling - and toasts per rejected file. Deleting the dead ReturnOrderItemModal is cleanup still pending.

getNotificationRedirectUrl returns quickLink only when it is a same-origin path or an absolute http(s) URL; the notifications page opens the absolute form through window.open with noopener and noreferrer as FirebaseInitializer does.
Avatar picker runs rejectImage and toasts on rejection. The check lives in src/helpers/imageUpload.ts so the return flow and the avatar share one validator.

images.remotePatterns is now derived from NEXT_PUBLIC_ADMIN_PANEL_URL plus an optional NEXT_PUBLIC_IMAGE_HOSTS list instead of the ** wildcard. dangerouslyAllowSVG left on with contentDispositionType attachment - residual risk noted.

Re-verified against the panel: MarketService::byActiveCode looks the code up and requires status ACTIVE so an unknown value like ZZ-ARBITRARY resolves to null and the chain falls through to the default market. The ZZ-ARBITRARY observation proved forwarding only - not that it was honoured. Residual accepted by the owner: a customer can set the cookie to another REAL active market code and browse and price in it since the header outranks fromAuthUser. Checkout deliverability is the backstop. Order money fields snapshot the request market at OrderService:845 rather than re-deriving it from the delivery address.
serializeJsonLd escapes < and > and & at the single emission point in DynamicSEO so a seller-authored value cannot close the script element.
resolveMarketForCountry now invalidates every market-scoped SWR key (settings, products, categories, brands, stores, home-layout, infinite-data, search, seller-reviews) instead of only /settings.
PROTECTED_ROUTES is a prefix match covering /cart (with /cart/checkout) and /payment.

Owner decision: the storefront ships as a static export, so an httpOnly token cookie would have to come from the API on another origin (SameSite=None + CORS credentials + Sanctum cookie auth) and would touch the mobile clients. Accepted as-is.
process.exit removed; success and failure paths share clearLocalSession so the browser session is always cleared.
login, register, verify-user and forget-password already post their payload as the request body.
redux-persist transform strips access_token on write and restores it from the session cookie on rehydrate, so localStorage holds no usable credential.
Offline cart keeps any item the server rejected instead of clearing the whole cart on a partial sync.
ensureIdempotencyKey keeps one key per checkout attempt, reusing it across retries and minting a new one only when the payment method changes.
Profile SSR returns null plus an error flag on failure and the page renders ErrorState with retry instead of a blank editable form.
useInfiniteData already throws when the response is unsuccessful so SWR records the error.

The empty-cart branch reads a machine-readable code when the panel sends one and falls back to the message match, so a transport failure can never clear the cart. Panel-side code field flagged, not added.
The hidden-button click and the window.showFailedItemsModal global are gone; failed sync items now live in a cartNotice slice and the removed-items modal opens off cart state alone.
SSR handlers return stable error codes (SSR_ERROR_CODES) that the pages resolve through translateErrorCode; keys added to all three locales.

The recharge ceiling is now a documented WALLET_MAX_RECHARGE constant instead of a bare literal. A per-market limit needs a wallet setting on the panel - flagged rather than added, per the API-contract rule.

Logout now clears the user-scoped localStorage keys (recent searches, shopping list, ad tracking queues); the FCM token stays because logout unbinds it server-side. Moving those features onto redux-persist is left as the larger refactor.
Swept every physical utility to its logical twin - ml/mr/pl/pr to ms/me/ps/pe and text-left/right to text-start/end - across 54 files, including negative margins. Zero physical utilities remain.
All 20 unlabelled icon-only controls in shipped screens carry an aria-label from new a11y.* keys in en, hi and ar. The two left are in the design-system sandbox page.
Added an ErrorBoundary mounted in _app.tsx rendering ErrorState with retry, plus a styled and translated 500 page.
The profile page reads the user from Redux with the SSR prop as the seed, so its own refresh reaches the UI.
The checkout re-syncs its selected-address copy against the address list on every load and clears the selection when the address is gone.
A location change revalidates only market-scoped keys instead of every mounted SWR key.
Anonymous server-side settings reads go through a 60-second per-market memo, so repeated SSR navigations stop re-fetching the payload.
The cart refresh moved out of the finally block to the failure branches only, so a successful order no longer refetches after navigating away.
